meta.note: Primary items quote the Supreme Court's own record of proceedings or judgment, or a High Court order. Press items quote the report as fetched on 2026-10-09; the court's order was not found.

items.case: Mahua Moitra v. Election Commission of India (writ petition, Supreme Court)
items.headline: Trinamool MP Mahua Moitra moves Supreme Court against electoral roll revision in Bihar
items.claim: Trinamool Congress MP Mahua Moitra asked the Supreme Court to quash the Commission's order of 24 June 2025 and to stop it from ordering the same revision in other states, LiveLaw reported.
items.quote: a direction to quash the Order dated 24.06.2025 issued by Election Commission of India ... restraining Election Commission of India from issuing similar orders for Special Intensive Revision

items.case: Association for Democratic Reforms & Ors. v. Election Commission of India, Diary No. 35785 of 2025, with six other petitions
items.headline: Petitions against the Bihar revision listed for 10 July
items.claim: Counsel for ADR and other petitioners mentioned seven petitions against the Bihar revision, and the Court let them be filed during the vacation and listed them for 10 July 2025.
items.quote: Leave to file the petition(s) during Partial Court Working Days is granted, with an advance copy of the petition(s) to be given to the appropriate authorities. List the petitions on 10.07.2025 [Thursday].

items.outlet: Supreme Court of India (judgment of 27.05.2026, 2026 INSC 564, para 10.8)
items.case: Association for Democratic Reforms & Ors. v. Election Commission of India, W.P.(C) No. 640 of 2025 and connected petitions
items.headline: Notice issued, and three questions framed
items.claim: The Court issued notice to the Commission and said the petitions raised three questions about its power, its method and the timing before the Bihar election, according to the account in the Court's 2026 judgment.
items.quote: Upon hearing the parties on 10.07.2025, this Court, while issuing notice to the Commission, observed that on a prima facie appraisal, three substantial questions arise for determination: first, the very authority of the Commission to embark upon the impugned exercise; second, the procedure and methodology adopted in carrying out the exercise, including the method prescribed by the Commission to ascertain the Citizenship of the Voters; and third, the propriety of its timing

items.case: Association for Democratic Reforms & Ors. v. Election Commission of India, W.P.(C) No. 640 of 2025 and connected petitions
items.headline: The list of 65 lakh names to be published with reasons
items.claim: The Court recorded the Commission's agreement to publish, district by district and searchable by EPIC number, the list of about 65 lakh electors left off the Bihar draft roll with the reason for each.
items.quote: The list of 65,00,000 (approximate) voters, whose names appeared in the Voter List as on 2025 but are not included in the Draft Roll dated 01.08.2025, shall be displayed on the websites of the District Election Officers (District-wise).

items.case: Association for Democratic Reforms & Ors. v. Election Commission of India, W.P.(C) No. 640 of 2025 and connected petitions
items.headline: Aadhaar to be accepted as the 12th document
items.claim: The Court directed the Commission to accept Aadhaar as proof of identity for the Bihar revision and said it is no proof of citizenship.
items.quote: Accordingly, we direct the Election Commission of India and its authorities to accept Aadhar Card as a proof of identity for the purpose of inclusion or exclusion in the revised voter list of the State of Bihar. Aadhaar Card, for this purpose, shall be treated as the 12th document by the Authorities.

items.case: W.P.(C) No. 855 of 2025, tagged with Association for Democratic Reforms & Ors. v. Election Commission of India, W.P.(C) No. 640 of 2025 and connected petitions
items.headline: A petition in support of the revision
items.claim: The Court issued notice on 8 September 2025 on W.P.(C) 855 of 2025, which its 2026 judgment describes as a petition asking for such revisions to be held at regular intervals.
items.quote: We deem it appropriate to clarify that certain petitions (for instance, Writ Petition (Civil) No. 855 of 2025) have in fact been instituted in support of the SIR exercise. The Petitioner(s) in these cases have urged that such an exercise ought to be conducted at regular intervals to prevent and curb the inclusion of ineligible persons in the electoral rolls on account of illegal influx.

items.case: B Sathyanarayanan v. The Chief Election Commissioner and Another, W.P. No. 39744 of 2025, Madras High Court
items.headline: SIR of Tamil Nadu electoral rolls will begin in a week, Election Commission tells Madras High Court
items.claim: A former AIADMK MLA asked the Madras High Court to order a re-verification of 229 booths in T. Nagar, and the Court adjourned the case after the Commission said the revision would begin within a week, LiveLaw reported.
items.quote: The court took note of the submissions and adjourned the case by a week.

items.case: Public interest litigation on the SIR in West Bengal, Calcutta High Court
items.headline: Calcutta High Court asks EC to submit affidavit on PIL challenging SIR in West Bengal
items.claim: A PIL asked the Calcutta High Court to have the West Bengal revision use the current roll in place of the 2002 roll and to protect booth level officers, and the Court asked the Commission for an affidavit, The Week reported.
items.quote: The court ordered ECI to file a short affidavit within 10 days on November 18 on the need for the SIR in West Bengal.

items.case: Petitions of the DMK, CPI(M), West Bengal Congress and Trinamool Congress leaders against the order of 27 October 2025, Supreme Court
items.headline: Supreme Court seeks ECI's response on pleas challenging SIR in Tamil Nadu, West Bengal
items.claim: The Court issued notice on the petitions against the second phase in Tamil Nadu and West Bengal and asked the High Courts to hold back their own cases on the revision, The Leaflet reported.
items.quote: we request the jurisdictional High Courts to keep in abeyance or defer the writ proceedings

items.case: State of Kerala v. Election Commission of India, 2025 SCC OnLine Ker 12336, Kerala High Court
items.headline: Kerala HC refuses to entertain State's plea to defer SIR leaving it open to approach Supreme Court
items.claim: The Kerala government asked the High Court to put off the revision until the local body elections ended, and the Court dismissed the petition because the Supreme Court had asked High Courts to hold back such cases, SCC Online reported.
items.quote: judicial discipline and comity also require the Court to refrain from entertaining the writ petition

items.case: Petition of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) on booth level officers, Supreme Court
items.headline: Supreme Court issues directions to ease BLO workload in SIR exercise
items.claim: On a TVK petition saying 35 to 40 booth level officers had died under work pressure, the Court told states to provide more staff and cut working hours, National Herald reported.
items.quote: governments cannot remain indifferent when BLOs are pushed to the brink

items.case: State of Kerala and political party leaders v. Election Commission of India, Supreme Court
items.headline: Supreme Court defers plea to extend Kerala SIR deadline, posts on December 18
items.claim: The Kerala government and leaders of the IUML, Congress and CPI(M) asked for more time for enumeration forms, and the Court put off a decision to 18 December, LiveLaw reported.
items.quote: will take a call then on whether to pass further extension

items.case: PIL No. 1272 of 2025, Allahabad High Court
items.headline: Allahabad High Court rejects PIL to adopt ECI's SIR guidelines for UP three-tier panchayat roll revision
items.claim: A PIL asked the Allahabad High Court to apply the Commission's revision guidelines to Uttar Pradesh's panchayat rolls, and the Court dismissed it, LiveLaw reported.
items.quote: there is absolutely no reason for this Court to interfere

items.case: W.P.(C) No. 1089 of 2025 and connected petitions (SIR matters related to the State of West Bengal)
items.headline: Names in the logical discrepancy list to be displayed
items.claim: The Court recorded that about 1.40 crore people in West Bengal had been sent notices and directed that names in the logical discrepancy list be displayed at panchayat, block and ward offices.
items.quote: The names of the persons figuring in the logical discrepancies may be displayed at the Gram Panchayat Bhawans, public places in every Taluka and Block Office of every Taluka (Sub-Division), as well as in the Ward Offices in the cities of the urban areas.

items.case: W.P.(C) No. 1089 of 2025 and connected petitions (SIR matters related to the State of West Bengal), with Mamata Banerjee's W.P.(C) No. 129 of 2026
items.headline: 8,505 state officers to assist the registration officers
items.claim: The order records that Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee appeared in her own petition on 4 February 2026, and the Court directed the 8,505 officers the state offered to report to the district officers.
items.quote: Let the State Government ensure that all 8505 Group B officers/officials, whose list was handed over to the Court today, report to the District Electoral Officers/EROs by 5:00 p.m. tomorrow.

items.case: Special civil application by two Surat Congress office-bearers, Gujarat High Court
items.headline: Gujarat HC moved against voter list revisions
items.claim: The Surat district Congress president and a Seva Dal organiser asked the Gujarat High Court to reject objections not filed under the rules, to act against false objections and to halt the revision, LawTrend reported.
items.quote: is expected to be heard shortly by a bench comprising Justice Bhargav Karia and Justice L.S. Pirzada

items.case: Petition by 91 displaced residents of Akbar Nagar, Lucknow, W.P.(C) No. 191 (as reported), Supreme Court
items.headline: Supreme Court declines to entertain plea of displaced Lucknow Akbar Nagar residents over voter roll exclusion
items.claim: Residents displaced by a 2023 demolition said they were left out of the Uttar Pradesh revision, and the Court sent them to the district election officer with liberty to go to the Allahabad High Court, Verdictum reported.
items.quote: We direct the District Election Commissioner, Lucknow to ascertain the facts of the case and take a decision as per the law.

items.case: W.P.(C) No. 1089 of 2025 and connected petitions (SIR matters related to the State of West Bengal)
items.headline: Appeals to tribunals of former judges
items.claim: The Court recorded that over 10,16,000 objections had been decided by judicial officers and directed that appeals go to tribunals of former Chief Justices and judges.
items.quote: our order dated 24.02.2026, in no uncertain terms, points out that the orders passed by the judicial officers will not be subjected to appeal before any Executive/Administrative Officer.

items.case: Suo Motu W.P.(C) No. 3 of 2026, In Re: Safety and Security of Judicial Officers Deputed for Work Relating to SIR of Electoral Rolls in the State of West Bengal
items.headline: Court acts after judicial officers are surrounded in Maldah
items.claim: After seven judicial officers deciding SIR claims were held at a BDO office in Maldah, the Court ordered central forces for them and asked the Commission to give the inquiry to the CBI or the NIA.
items.quote: The ECI is directed for requisitioning of adequate central forces and for their deployment at all places where the judicial officers have been deputed for adjudication of objections under the SIR process.

items.case: W.P.(C) No. 1089 of 2025 and connected petitions (SIR matters related to the State of West Bengal), with W.P.(C) No. 462 of 2026
items.headline: A pending appeal gives no vote
items.claim: On petitions from people deleted after the judicial officers' check, the Court directed that appeals decided before polling go into a supplementary roll and said a pending appeal gave no right to vote.
items.quote: However, it goes without saying that the mere pendency of appeals preferred by excluded persons before the Appellate Tribunals shall not entitle them to exercise their right to vote.

items.case: W.P.(C) No. 1089 of 2025 and connected petitions (SIR matters related to the State of West Bengal)
items.headline: West Bengal SIR: SC pushes SIR disputes to Calcutta HC as appeal backlog mounts
items.claim: Counsel told the Court that 136 of nearly 27 lakh appeals had been decided, and the Court declined fresh grievances and sent the parties to the Chief Justice of the Calcutta High Court, Supreme Court Observer reported.
items.quote: Please approach the Chief Justice of the Calcutta High Court.

items.case: Association for Democratic Reforms & Ors. v. Election Commission of India, W.P.(C) No. 640 of 2025 and connected petitions
items.headline: The Supreme Court upholds the Bihar revision
items.claim: The Court held the Bihar revision lawful under section 21(3) of the Representation of the People Act read with Article 324 and said declining to enrol someone does not declare that person not to be a citizen.
items.quote: It does not amount to a declaration that the individual is not a citizen of India; it merely reflects the Commission’s inability to be satisfied, for electoral purposes, that the statutory conditions are met.

items.outlet: Supreme Court of India (2026 INSC 564, para 186(h))
items.case: Association for Democratic Reforms & Ors. v. Election Commission of India, W.P.(C) No. 640 of 2025 and connected petitions
items.headline: Citizenship cases to the competent authority, and judicial review for wrong deletions
items.claim: The Court directed the Commission to refer within four weeks the cases it deleted as non-citizens to the authority under the Citizenship Act and allowed people in Bihar wrongly deleted as absent, dead, shifted or duplicate to seek judicial review.
items.quote: Regarding persons whose names have been deleted from the 2003 roll on account of the Commission being of the opinion that they are not citizens, the Commission shall refer such cases within 4 weeks to the Competent authority under the Citizenship Act, 1955, for adjudication of their citizenship.

items.outlet: High Court for the State of Telangana (order reproduced by LiveLaw)
items.case: Writ Petition No. 20188 of 2026
items.headline: Deleted voter told to use the SIR
items.claim: A Charminar voter asked the High Court to restore his family's deleted names, and the Court dismissed the petition and told him to use the revision then under way.
items.quote: Therefore, the petitioner is at liberty to participate in the process of SIR in respect of his grievances relating to deletion of his name and the names of his family members from the electoral rolls earlier. This court, therefore, is not inclined to interfere in the instant writ petition.

items.case: Writ petition by Adivasi Sena, Telangana High Court
items.headline: Telangana HC seeks response on plea against non-tribal voters in Scheduled Areas
items.claim: Adivasi Sena asked the Telangana High Court to have ineligible non-tribal voters removed from the rolls of the Fifth Schedule Areas during the revision, and the Court sought replies, Telangana Today reported.
items.quote: directed the respondents to file their counters within two weeks

items.case: Batch of writ petitions on G.O.Ms. No. 172, Telangana High Court
items.headline: Telangana HC takes up plea on Family Register Certificate as voter eligibility proof
items.claim: Petitioners asked the Telangana High Court to strike the state's Family Register Certificate from the revision's list of documents, and the Court gave the Commission time and listed the case for 12 August, Telangana Today reported.
items.quote: cannot be treated as a valid eligibility document for voter enrollment under the Special Intensive Revision

items.case: PIL on homeless and demolition-displaced voters, Delhi High Court
items.headline: Delhi SIR: plea to include homeless and demolition-displaced voters
items.claim: A PIL asked the Delhi High Court for special arrangements so homeless and displaced people could enrol in the revision, and the Court reserved its order and said it would not monitor the policy, LiveLaw reported.
items.quote: everything cannot be thrust upon courts

items.case: Writ petition by a deleted elector working abroad, Calcutta High Court
items.headline: Calcutta High Court directs SIR tribunal to expeditiously decide plea of Saudi resident unable to renew passport over voter list deletion
items.claim: A man deleted in the revision said it was blocking his passport renewal, and the Calcutta High Court told the appellate tribunal to decide his appeal within two weeks without going into the merits, LiveLaw reported.
items.quote: directed the concerned SIR Appellate Tribunal to dispose of the pending appeal within two weeks

items.case: Devender Yadav & Anr v. Election Commission of India & Anr, 2026 LiveLaw (Del) 835, Delhi High Court
items.headline: Delhi SIR: High Court refuses to entertain plea against first-time applicant declaration for deleted voters, says file PIL
items.claim: Delhi Congress president Devender Yadav challenged the Form 6 declaration that deleted voters must sign as first-time applicants, and he withdrew the petition after the Court told him to file it as a PIL, LiveLaw reported.
items.quote: The plea was accordingly withdrawn.

items.case: Petition of two transparency activists under Article 32, Supreme Court
items.headline: Delhi SIR: SC says notices going to people mechanically, asks EC to adopt additional safeguards
items.claim: Two transparency activists who had petitioned the Court asked for the list of Delhi voters sent notices and the criteria for logical discrepancies, and the bench told the Commission to look at extra safeguards, ThePrint reported.
items.quote: The notices are going to people almost mechanically. Just look whether some additional safeguards are needed.

items.case: W.P.(Crl.) No. 401 of 2026, against decisions of the Chief Election Commissioner, Supreme Court
items.headline: Supreme Court says modified Form 6 not approved by it
items.claim: A petition asked the Court to quash 14 decisions it said the Chief Election Commissioner took alone, and the Court issued notice, tagged it with a similar case and said it had not approved any modified Form 6, LiveLaw reported.
items.quote: Any modified Form 6 has not been approved by us. Let's be clear.

items.case: Writ Petition No. 732 of 2026, a family's petition on deletion after Form 8, Bombay High Court at Goa
items.headline: 'No Business Asking Them to Fill Form 6 Because System Didn't Allow Form 8': Bombay HC Condemns ECI's Handling of SIR Process
items.claim: A family of six who moved house within the same constituency filed Form 8 and were then deleted from the roll, because the ERONET software found no record of their cards and allowed only a rejection. The bench asked the Commission to show where the law allows a deletion without a hearing and said the family should not have been asked to file Form 6, The Wire reported, citing The Times of India.
items.quote: Questioning the legality of the removal of the Santa Cruz family from the voter list without a hearing, the bench noted, "Show us from the Act where it empowers you to delete without hearing. If you are planning to remove someone's name, you have to give the person an opportunity of hearing first." ... According to TOI, the bench replied, "You have no business asking them to fill Form 6 because the system didn't allow you to do it on Form 8. That was the problem."
items.response: The Wire reported that the Commission's counsel said other voters removed in the same way had been put back on the roll after filing Form 6, and that the family had not filed Form 6 when asked to.
items.note: PTI via Telangana Today (1 Oct 2026, 11:18 AM) agrees on the hearing date (Wednesday 30 Sept), the bench, the six family members in Santa Cruz, Form 8, ERONET offering only 'reject', and the bench's 'Show us from the Act...what empowers you to delete without hearing?'. It adds that the court said the draft roll cannot be the basis for deletion. It does not carry the 'no business' line, which The Wire attributes to TOI. Both sources name the petitioner; the draft does not.

items.case: Writ Petition No. 732 of 2026, a family's petition on deletion after Form 8, Bombay High Court at Goa
items.headline: 'What Is SIR's Purpose If Citizens Are Being Removed From Voter's List? Bombay High Court Asks ECI
items.claim: At a further hearing of the same family's petition the bench asked what purpose the revision served if citizens were left off the roll. It also asked why a voter who had moved house should have to sign the enumeration form, whose declaration says the voter still lives at the address on the existing roll, LiveLaw reported.
items.quote: "Read the judgment, it says ECI has an obligation to ensure that all Indian citizens are on the list... If citizens are excluded what will we do with your SIR? If citizens are being removed from the list then what is the purpose of this entire SIR process then?" ... "If a voter comes to you with Form 8, saying he has changed his address you just cannot tell that person that look your name isn't included in the draft roll now you will have to fill in Form 6 (inclusion of new voter). Your enumeration form, basically has a declaration that a person continues to live in the address as mentioned in the existing voters list. But consider, if someone has changed their residence, can you compel the person to make a false declaration by submitting that pre-filled enumeration? Why can't that person simply give a Form 8 because anyway, his name is there in the existing list he just wants to get his address changed.. Why compel enumeration form?" Justice Menezes observed.
items.response: LiveLaw reported that the Commission's counsel argued that a voter had to submit the enumeration form along with Form 8 to have an address changed, and that a voter who did not submit it had to file Form 6.

items.case: Petition on the implementation of the SIR in Maharashtra, Bombay High Court
items.headline: Maharashtra SIR: Bombay High Court Declines Oral Plea To Restrain ECI From Deleting Voters' Names, Says SC Seized Of Issue
items.claim: The Chief Justice's bench refused an oral request to order that no names be deleted from the roll in Maharashtra for the time being. It said it would follow the Supreme Court, which it was told had restrained High Courts in November 2025 from hearing petitions on the revision, and adjourned the case by four weeks, LiveLaw reported. The petition asks for the order and reasons behind the revision in the state and for safeguards against wrongful exclusion.
items.quote: "There are restraining orders already... No purpose will be served by a parallel litigation. Let the SC hear the matter first and we will consider it later," Chief Justice said. ... The judges turned down the said oral prayer, by observing, "No no no...we are not going to pass any such orders... We will follow judicial propriety." The bench accordingly, adjourned the hearing for four weeks.
items.note: LiveLaw gives no case number. The petition alleges BLOs in Maharashtra asked for supporting documents with enumeration forms; that is the petitioners' allegation and is left out of the claim.
